notes.decision: Read as Lyc. ⲉⲧⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ qualitative of ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ 'be prepared, made ready.' Translates as 'which is prepared.' The construction ⲉⲧⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ = 'which is prepared there for them.'
Read ⲣⲟⲱⲃ as ⲣ̄-ϩⲱⲃ 'do work, labor' with vowel-doubling and ϩ-loss characteristic of Lycopolitan. The construction is conjunctive 2pl 'and that you should labor in the Spirit.'

ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ tentatively read as Lyc. variant of ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' in agricultural sense 'sow seed.' 'Land of sowing/casting' fits the harvesting-fruit context of the closing kephalaion. Could alternatively be a plowing-term.

Chapter-heading: 'the three begettings of the flesh.' ⲭⲡⲟ = Lyc. for ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, generation' (cf. ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲭⲧⲟ in glossary). The three modes enumerated in lines 8-11: (a) begotten in [union] with abortions, (b) begotten in abortions, (c) self-molded — the standard Manichaean taxonomy of fleshly origins.

ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲩϩⲉ = ⲛⲍⲟⲩⲍⲉ 'abortions' (in glossary) with regular ϩ/ⲍ orthographic variation. The Manichaean myth of archonic abortions falling to earth is the controlling cosmological context — the second class of fleshly begetting comes from these.
Read 3pl present 'they mold themselves alone' — the third class of begetting: self-formed entities. πλάσσειν here used reflexively for autogeneration, distinct from human procreative begetting (ⲭⲡⲟ).

Standard Kephalaia narrative-frame: ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ (Lyc. for ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said') + ⲡⲛ̄-ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'our Illuminator.' The 1pl possessive ⲡⲛ̄- is the disciples' communal address. Cf. glossary entries ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ and ⲡⲡⲛ̄ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ.
Tentatively read as a form on ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, judge' (cf. ⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ 'reckon them' in glossary). Possibly verbal 'their reckoning/their being-counted.' Confidence low given heavy surrounding lacunae.
